MIND. [1] [Ars. h.]
Excited ; wants to talk constantly. θ Yellow fever.
   

SENSORIUM. [2] [Ars. h.]
Stupefying feeling in head, as of a load there. --F. W. Payne.
   

UPPER FACE. [8] [Ars. h.]
The face looks old, and bears an expression of pain. --F. W. Payne.
Face greatly changed. θ Yellow fever.
Countenance wears an expression of extreme anxiety. θ Collapse of cholera.
   

TEETH AND GUMS. [10] [Ars. h.]
Sore bleeding gums around remaining root of right upper incisor. --C. Hg.
   

APPETITE, THIRST. DESIRES, AVERSIONS. [14] [Ars. h.]
Loss of appetite. --F. W. Payne.
   

EATING AND DRINKING. [15] [Ars. h.]
Constant retching and vomiting after taking the least thing to eat or drink. θ Yellow fever.
   

HICCOUGH, BELCHING, NAUSEA AND VOMITING. [16] [Ars. h.]
Uninterrupted belching up, spasmodically, of a large quantity of tasteless air, with great pain in abdomen. θ Yellow fever.
Very troublesome and annoying hiccough. θ Yellow fever.
Nausea. θ Yellow fever.
Vomiting of mucous, yellow, green and bitter fluid. θ Yellow fever.
   

ABDOMEN AND LOINS. [19] [Ars. h.]
Abdomen burning, outside ; cold feet. θ Yellow fever.
   

STOOLS AND RECTUM. [20] [Ars. h.]
Obstinate constipation. --Eisenmenger. (Called "obstinate" by the Old School, which is transferring a quality of their own mind to the colon.)
Constipation, with a feeling of heaviness and stiffness, like a weight in abdomen. --F. W. Payne.
   

URINARY ORGANS. [21] [Ars. h.]
Pressure in kidneys, extending to shoulder blades, with pain in region of kidneys during desire to urinate. θ Yellow fever.
Urine dark, blackish-red, with pure blood. θ Yellow fever.
Discharge at times of large quantities of pale urine. F. W. Payne.
   

VOICE AND LARYNX. TRACHEA AND BRONCHIA. [25] [Ars. h.]
His customary hawking up of phlegm ceases ; 6th day. --F. K.
   

HEART, PULSE AND CIRCULATION. [29] [Ars. h.]
Pulse frequent. θ Yellow fever.
Pulse quite imperceptible. θ Collapse in cholera.
   

NECK AND BACK. [31] [Ars. h.]
Pain as if something was sticking below right shoulder blade ; increased at first, and disappeared after three hours' sleep. --C. Hg.
   

LIMBS IN GENERAL. [34] [Ars. h.]
Coldness of limbs. --F. W. Payne.
   

NERVES. [36] [Ars. h.]
Great prostration and general malaise. --F. W. Payne.
   

SLEEP. [37] [Ars. h.]
Total sleeplessness. θ Yellow fever.
Sleeplessness. --F. W. Payne. (A chronic case. See 47.)
   

TEMPERATURE AND WEATHER. [39] [Ars. h.]
General chilliness on slight exposure, or change of temperature. Payne.
   

FEVER. [40] [Ars. h.]
Much heat and burning in different parts of body, particularly over renal region. --F. W. Payne.
Surface of body bedewed with moisture, with unnatural warm feel of such cases. θ Collapse of cholera.
   

ATTACKS, PERIODICITY. [41] [Ars. h.]
Typhus tertianus postponens. Death on 9th day. --Gehlen. Bullock.
   

TISSUES. [44] [Ars. h.]
Collapse in cholera Asiatica.
   

SKIN. [46] [Ars. h.]
Dark brown skin all over. θ Yellow fever.
Dark brown, sallow look of skin. --F. W. Payne.
